en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, West Wildwood, Cape May County, New Jersey, September 1921, Sheet 99

properties.name: A Avenue / Bay Avenue / West Poplar Avenue

sheet-99.description: The whole of West Wildwood as it stood in September 1921, drawn on a single new sheet at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The borough occupies a narrow island between Grassy Sound to the east and north and a tidal channel to the west. Its core is a regular grid: West Pine, West Maple, West Glenwood and West Poplar Avenues run down the sheet, crossed by the lettered Avenues B to G and by Neptune Avenue, with Magnolia Avenue below Neptune. West of West Pine Avenue a wedge between the street and the railroad holds a second set of lettered streets, Avenues H, I and J, and blocks lettered A, B and C. At the north end Avenue A and Bay Avenue run diagonally along the shore, and beyond the railroad Eocene Road and a second Bay Avenue serve long rows of narrow lots along the west channel. The W. & D. B. Shore Line (Reading) crosses the island on an embankment from lower left to upper right, with a railroad station near the north end. Development is almost entirely small frame dwellings, most of them along West Glenwood and West Poplar Avenues; many platted lots are still empty. Named buildings are the West Wildwood Casino on the Grassy Sound shore, a fire department and volunteer company house with a combined motor engine, a woodworking shop and store houses beside the railroad. A four-inch water pipe is marked along West Glenwood Avenue. Across Wildwood Canal on the right, a separate strip of platted but undeveloped lots lines West 26th Avenue and Bay Road between the canal and Grassy Sound; it has no cross street.
notes: Avenue A to Avenue G east of West Pine Avenue are today A Avenue to G Avenue; West Pine, West Maple, West Glenwood and West Poplar Avenues keep their names.
Avenues H, I and J west of West Pine Avenue do not correspond to modern H, I and J Avenues, which lie south of Neptune Avenue; they were not used as control.
The railroad is lettered W. & D. B. Shore Line (Reading); OpenStreetMap has no running line on it today.

The West 26th Avenue and Bay Road strip across Wildwood Canal has no cross street and is placed by the fit of the main grid; modern West 26th Avenue projects onto the drawn street line but begins about 100 m beyond the bottom edge of the sheet, so the platted strip north of it is not built today.

West Wildwood, printed sheet 99 of New Jersey coast vol. 4, new sheet Sept. 1921, 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper right (rotation about 46 deg). One part: Avenues A to J, Neptune Av, W. Pine, W. Maple, W. Glenwood, W. Poplar Avs, Bay Av, Eocene Rd, W. & D. B. Shore Line (Reading), and across Wildwood Canal a strip of lots on W. 26th Av and Bay Rd with no cross street. Lettered avenues west of W. Pine (H, I, J) do not match the modern lettering and were left out.
